516a2ee955e1b623f0ba903a3e9749c1250d8b2f.summary: Year-end review by the Intezer security blog of Linux threats in 2020, not a single-incident report. It says APTs have long targeted Linux, mainly attributed to Russia, China and North Korea, and that a Linux version of WellMail was disclosed in July, attributed by the UK NCSC to APT29. Cybercrime groups also moved to Linux, including a Linux TrickBot sample and IPStorm, and existing tools such as Penquin (Turla) and QNAPCrypt were updated. Golang is highlighted for cross-platform malware that is hard for antivirus engines to detect, with a Carbanak Linux sample as an example. The post ends…

51672fafe669cf99d78fbf7393084e04cf008325.summary: Mandiant report on UNC3886, a suspected China-nexus espionage actor that targets governments, telecoms, technology, aerospace and defense, and energy sectors. It covers zero-day exploits in VMware and Fortinet products, publicly available rootkits (REPTILE, MEDUSA) for persistence, backdoored SSH software and a backdoored TACACS+ server for credential theft, malware using GitHub and Google Drive as C2 channels, and VMCI-based backdoors. Mandiant tracks the activity as Campaign 23-022 since March 2023, with victims mainly in North America, Southeast Asia and Oceania.

5183b51959c244b3215f7e95e1560241e7e9a34a.summary: ANSSI reports an intrusion campaign against Centreon monitoring software that breached several French entities, mostly information technology providers, especially web hosting providers. Compromised Centreon servers ran a P.A.S. 3.1.4 webshell and an Exaramel backdoor. ANSSI says the campaign bears several similarities to earlier Sandworm campaigns, but the initial compromise method is not known. The report gives detection methods and recommendations. The activity is dated from late 2017 to 2020.

5166e89de3f941b0303e4cb108b0366e2d2a17db.summary: A BleepingComputer report (December 2023) says the LockBit ransomware operation was recruiting affiliates and developers from BlackCat/ALPHV and NoEscape after both suffered disruptions and NoEscape affiliates alleged an exit scam. LockBitSupp reportedly told affiliates they could use LockBit's leak site and negotiation panel to keep extorting victims. The report notes one BlackCat victim had appeared on LockBit's leak site, and says it is too early to tell whether affiliates are moving, though another rebrand may follow. Law enforcement involvement in the ALPHV outage was reported but not…
